question: What is the outermost layer of the skin called?

options.A: Subcutaneous layer
options.B: Dermis
options.C: Hypodermis
options.D: Epidermis

explanation: The epidermis is the outermost, superficial layer of the skin made of epithelial tissue. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h1)

question: What causes stretch marks, or striae gravidarum, during pregnancy?

options.A: Fungal infections growing under tight clothing
options.B: Blockage of sweat glands by high hormone levels
options.C: Accumulation of excess subcutaneous fat deposits
options.D: Breaking of elastic fibers in the dermis from rapid stretching

explanation: As the belly grows quickly, the elastic fibers in the deeper skin layer stretch and tiny breaks happen, leading to stretch marks. Completely normal!

question: How does metformin mainly work to help manage Type 2 diabetes?

options.A: Triggering direct beta cell regeneration within the exocrine pancreas
options.B: Decreasing liver glucose production and improving insulin sensitivity
options.C: Stimulating immediate renal excretion of all circulating blood proteins
options.D: Blocking carbohydrate digestion enzymes inside the small intestine

explanation: Metformin is a classic drug you'll see everywhere in wards! It works mainly by stopping the liver from releasing too much extra sugar and helping your body's cells respond better to natural insulin.

question: Which of these is a major characteristic of adult learners during a teaching session?

options.A: They refuse to participate in group discussions or role play
options.B: They remember long lists of medical terms better than children
options.C: They need strict discipline and constant supervision from lecturers
options.D: They prefer to be actively involved in planning their learning goals

explanation: Brilliant! Adults love having a say in what and how they learn. They value their independence rather than just sitting quietly as passive listeners.

question: Why should you quickly check on your patient right before you carry out a planned intervention?

options.A: To confirm that the planned action is still safe and necessary for them right now
options.B: To rewrite the entire medical diagnosis from the beginning
options.C: To make sure the physician is standing nearby to supervise the nursing care
options.D: To ensure that all hospital equipment has been paid for in advance

explanation: Patients change fast! What was a great plan an hour ago might need tweaking if their condition shifts. Always assess before you act.

question: Why are social programs like senior centers so helpful for older adults?

options.A: They provide free prescription drugs for chronic illnesses
options.B: They offer round-the-clock intensive nursing care
options.C: They replace the need for regular medical checkups
options.D: They reduce isolation and promote mental well-being

explanation: Getting together for social activities helps seniors make friends, stay happy, and chase away loneliness.

question: What decides how thick or watery a colostomy stool will be?

options.A: The anatomical location of the stoma along the large intestine
options.B: The amount of physical exercise the patient does every day
options.C: The time of day the patient eats their main meal
options.D: The exact brand of the appliance pouch the patient wears

explanation: Exactly! Stool gets thicker the longer it travels through the colon because more water is absorbed along the way.

question: Why is it so important to involve a speech-language pathologist early after a brain injury?

options.A: To prescribe appropriate mobility braces and walking frames
options.B: To coordinate home healthcare insurance and discharge funding
options.C: To manage chronic joint pain and muscle spasms in the limbs
options.D: To check for safe swallowing before the patient eats or drinks

explanation: Safety first! SLPs make sure patients can swallow food and water without choking, while also helping them find ways to communicate their needs.

question: Why do we actually need dietary fats to absorb certain vitamins?

options.A: Fat binds directly to water-soluble vitamins
options.B: Fat makes the stomach produce more acid
options.C: Vitamins A, D, E, and K dissolve in fat
options.D: Fat stops the liver from destroying vitamins

explanation: Think of fat as the vehicle that carries vitamins A, D, E, and K through your gut so your body can use them. Without fat, these vitamins just pass right through!

question: What happens during passive health surveillance?

options.A: The government bans the collection of all health statistics
options.B: Nurses actively hunt for sick people in every single household
options.C: Patients diagnose themselves at home without telling anyone
options.D: Clinics routinely report disease cases upward to health authorities

explanation: In passive surveillance, we wait for patients to come to the clinic feeling unwell, and then our routine reports flow up to the health authorities. It's the standard way we track everyday illnesses!

question: Which of these is an ethical dilemma involving money in nursing?

options.A: Deciding which nurse gets to attend a fully funded overseas conference
options.B: Balancing hospital cost-cutting with the duty to advocate for patients
options.C: Reporting a colleague who forgot to wash their hands before a procedure
options.D: Choosing whether to buy electronic tablets or paper charts for the ward

explanation: This is a classic challenge: nurses always want the best for their patients, but must navigate strict financial limits set by management.

question: Which common household appliance is completely safe for a patient with a pacemaker to use?

options.A: Industrial arc welder
options.B: Microwave oven
options.C: High-power magnetic tool
options.D: Handheld security wand

explanation: Good news for patients—standard household microwaves are well-shielded and won't mess with modern pacemakers. One less thing to worry about!

question: What is the main job of the fallopian tubes in the female body?

options.A: To serve as the usual site for fertilization of the egg
options.B: To provide a muscular environment for fetal development
options.C: To secrete large amounts of protective progesterone
options.D: To produce the monthly supply of mature oocytes

explanation: You nailed it! The fallopian tubes catch the released egg and act as the meeting place where sperm usually fertilize it before it moves to the uterus.

question: What is another common name for the channels connecting the lateral ventricles to the third ventricle?

options.A: Aqueduct of Sylvius
options.B: Foramina of Monro
options.C: Foramen magnum
options.D: Apertures of Luschka

explanation: You got it! These little connecting channels are famously known as the foramina of Monro. Keep this handy for exams!

question: What does the letter 'M' stand for in the TNM cancer staging system?

options.A: Muscle involvement
options.B: Microscopic grading
options.C: Distant metastasis
options.D: Malignant potential

explanation: Spot on! In the TNM system, M tells us if the cancer has traveled (metastasized) to distant organs far away from where it started.

question: Which of these strategies directly helps nurses avoid burnout by giving them more control over their time?

options.A: Mandatory double shifts on weekends
options.B: Flexible scheduling options
options.C: Eliminating all scheduled meal breaks
options.D: Strictly fixed vacation blackouts

explanation: Giving nurses a say in their shifts helps them balance family, rest, and school—a huge shield against burnout!

question: What are the small bumps on the areola called that secrete a protective fluid?

options.A: Montgomery glands
options.B: Lymph nodes
options.C: Sweat glands
options.D: Thyroid follicles

explanation: Montgomery glands are sebaceous glands located on the areola that keep the skin lubricated and healthy. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h2)

question: What is considered the most reliable indicator of a patient's pain intensity?

options.A: The nurse's clinical observation of vital signs
options.B: The physical size and depth of the tissue injury
options.C: The family member's estimate of the discomfort
options.D: The patient's personal self-report

explanation: Pain is a subjective experience, making the direct word of the patient the single most reliable source of information. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h3)

question: A patient receiving neck radiation asks if they can use their favorite scented lotion on the area. What is the best reply?

options.A: Recommend using only approved, gentle, fragrance-free products to avoid further skin irritation
options.B: Suggest stopping all skin hygiene practices until the entire course of treatment finishes
options.C: Advise scrubbing the skin firmly with a washcloth before applying any cream or lotion
options.D: Encourage applying the scented lotion generously right before each radiation session

explanation: You're thinking like a caring nurse! Radiation makes skin very sensitive, so stick to mild, fragrance-free lotions approved by the care team.

question: Why is proper cold chain storage a big deal in the DRF supply chain?

options.A: To ensure that large bulk orders take up less physical warehouse space
options.B: To speed up the delivery time from the manufacturer to the hospital
options.C: To comply with tax laws regarding imported pharmaceutical goods
options.D: To prevent temperature-sensitive medications like vaccines from losing potency

explanation: Some medications (like vaccines and insulin) are fragile. If they get too warm, they lose their strength and won't work for the patient.

question: Which of the following is NOT a routine screening objective for inherited blood conditions in the community?

options.A: Providing immediate blood transfusions to healthy carriers
options.B: Raising public awareness about genetic counseling
options.C: Identifying carrier status before family planning
options.D: Detecting early signs of trait markers in newborns

explanation: Carriers of genetic blood traits are generally healthy and do not require blood transfusions. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h4)

question: What is a cardiovascular complication?

options.A: A side effect caused by taking too many vitamins
options.B: A normal reaction to doing heavy exercise
options.C: A brand new primary heart disease
options.D: A secondary problem that happens after initial heart or blood vessel damage

explanation: Think of a complication as a follow-up problem. When the heart or blood vessels are already damaged, other issues pop up because the body's normal coping systems get overwhelmed. You've got this!

question: What is the main job of a healthy fallopian tube?

options.A: To filter waste products from the pelvic cavity
options.B: To provide a pathway for the egg and the site for fertilization
options.C: To produce female hormones like estrogen and progesterone
options.D: To nourish the developing embryo throughout the entire pregnancy

explanation: Think of the fallopian tube as the highway where the egg travels and meets sperm for fertilization. Simple and straightforward!

question: As a nurse researcher, why would you choose to use qualitative interviews?

options.A: To measure exact physiological vital signs over time
options.B: To explore deep human experiences and personal perspectives
options.C: To test new pharmaceutical drugs on large populations
options.D: To calculate statistical averages of hospital stays

explanation: You've got this! Qualitative interviews are all about listening to patients' stories and feelings, rather than just crunching numbers. It's the human side of nursing research!

question: What is the absolute gold standard method to confirm an NG tube is sitting correctly?

options.A: Abdominal X-ray confirmation
options.B: Auscultating an air bolus over the stomach
options.C: Observing condensation inside the clear plastic tube
options.D: Checking if the patient can speak clearly

explanation: An X-ray never guesses! It gives you a clear picture of exactly where the tube tip is resting, making it the top gold standard.

question: What does a high D-dimer blood test result usually mean?

options.A: Blood clots have recently formed and broken down in the body
options.B: The patient is not eating enough iron
options.C: There are zero platelets left in the blood
options.D: There is a sudden bacterial infection in the blood

explanation: D-dimer is a leftover protein fragment when a clot dissolves. If it's high, it tells us clotting and breakdown have been happening recently.

question: Which of these is a WRONG practice when it comes to preventing poisoning?

options.A: Using clear labeling on all containers holding hazardous substances
options.B: Storing kerosene and bleach in empty soft drink bottles in the kitchen
options.C: Consulting qualified health workers before taking herbal concoctions
options.D: Keeping all pharmaceutical drugs locked up away from children

explanation: You got it! Putting dangerous chemicals in drink bottles is a recipe for disaster. Always keep them in their original, clearly labeled containers.

question: Which of these is an absolute 'no-go' (contraindication) for using mifepristone and misoprostol?

options.A: A gestational age of exactly four weeks
options.B: A previous uncomplicated vaginal delivery
options.C: A history of mild seasonal allergies
options.D: A confirmed or suspected ectopic pregnancy

explanation: Remember, medical abortion only works inside the uterus. If the pregnancy is outside the uterus (ectopic), these drugs won't work and it's a major emergency!

question: Why should a nurse manager care about keeping the ward staff motivated?

options.A: It allows the manager to reduce overall nursing salaries
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for hospital policies
options.C: It leads to safer patient care and better staff retention
options.D: It guarantees that nurses will never make charting errors

explanation: You got it! When nurses feel valued and motivated, patients get safer care, and people are much happier staying on the team.

question: What is the main purpose of tracheobronchial suctioning?

options.A: Removing secretions to keep the airway clear
options.B: Expanding collapsed lung alveoli directly
options.C: Measuring the exact lung capacity
options.D: Delivering high concentrations of oxygen

explanation: Suctioning is primarily performed to clear trapped mucus and fluids when a patient cannot cough them out independently. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h1)

question: Which symptom do pregnant women often report along with constipation?

options.A: Sudden loss of all body hair
options.B: Constant swelling of the eyelids
options.C: Abdominal bloating and cramping
options.D: Inability to hear high-pitched sounds

explanation: Correct! When gas and waste move slowly through the large bowel, it naturally leads to uncomfortable bloating and mild cramps.

question: Which sensory receptors deep in the skin are great at detecting deep pressure and heavy vibrations?

options.A: Pacinian corpuscles
options.B: Free nerve endings
options.C: Meissner corpuscles
options.D: Merkel discs

explanation: Spot on! Pacinian corpuscles are shaped like tiny onions and sit deep in the skin to sense firm pressure and vibrations.

question: What is the big advantage of organizing healthcare into different levels (primary, secondary, tertiary)?

options.A: It makes primary health clinics responsible for major surgical operations
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any communication between nurses and doctors
options.C: It restricts rural clients from ever accessing modern contraceptive methods
options.D: It ensures clients receive care at the appropriate facility matching their medical complexity

explanation: Leveling care makes sure simple things are handled locally, while complex cases go smoothly to places fully equipped for them.

question: How does a stuffy, overheated lecture hall usually affect nursing students?

options.A: It induces lethargy and reduces cognitive processing speed
options.B: It improves their ability to memorize pharmacology lists
options.C: It sharpens their critical thinking and speeds up clinical math
options.D: It causes immediate hearing loss during lectures

explanation: Poor ventilation and high temperatures make everyone sleepy, which slows down how fast our brains process information. Keep yourself hydrated during long classes!

question: What is a clear sign that an expectorant is working successfully?

options.A: The cough becomes more productive and brings up phlegm easily
options.B: The patient develops a high fever and chills overnight
options.C: The cough stops completely within ten minutes of the first dose
options.D: The lung sounds change from clear to heavy coarse crackles

explanation: You got it! Success means the patient can finally clear out that gunk easily instead of having a tight, dry, miserable chest.

question: What does decentralized decision-making mean in primary nursing?

options.A: Authority for clinical choices rests directly with the bedside nurse.
options.B: Nurse managers handle every single choice regarding patient hygiene.
options.C: All hospital decisions must be approved by the chief medical director.
options.D: Patients make all of their own medical treatment decisions alone.

explanation: Decentralized just means power is shared! The nurse right there at the bedside has the backing to make immediate, smart clinical choices for their patient.

question: Giving an injection or checking a pulse falls under which domain of learning?

options.A: Emotional domain
options.B: Cognitive domain
options.C: Psychomotor domain
options.D: Affective domain

explanation: The psychomotor domain is all about physical movement, coordination, and hands-on nursing procedures.

question: Which sign tells you a newborn baby is working too hard to breathe and has respiratory distress?

options.A: Sternal retractions
options.B: Acrocyanosis of hands
options.C: Coupled heart sounds
options.D: Active limb movement

explanation: When the skin pulls in around the chest bones (sternal retractions), it means the baby is struggling to pull air into their lungs. That's a classic warning sign!

question: Which bacteria is used as the main sign that water has been contaminated with feces?

options.A: Staphylococcus aureus
options.B: Escherichia coli
options.C: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.D: Lactobacillus acidophilus

explanation: Well done! E. coli normally lives in human and animal guts, so finding it in a water source is a clear red flag for fecal pollution.

question: Which special part of the kidney detects a drop in blood pressure and releases renin?

options.A: Juxtaglomerular apparatus
options.B: Collecting duct
options.C: Bowman's capsule
options.D: Loop of Henle

explanation: Nice work! The juxtaglomerular apparatus acts like the kidney's security guard, sensing low pressure and releasing renin to kick off the body's blood-pressure-raising system.

question: Why would a nurse need to flush or irrigate a patient's ear?

options.A: To drain excessive fluid from the middle ear cavity
options.B: To remove stuck earwax or small foreign objects
options.C: To repair a torn eardrum using pressurized water
options.D: To treat an active bacterial infection deep in the inner ear

explanation: Ear irrigation is a safe way to wash out stubborn wax buildup or little things that got stuck in the outer ear. Great clinical thinking!

question: What purpose does the cork bung serve when using a Nelson inhaler?

options.A: It filters out dust particles before the patient breathes the vapor
options.B: It seals the top of the jar so steam escapes only through the mouthpiece
options.C: It measures the exact temperature of the water inside the container
options.D: It absorbs excess medication that spills during preparation

explanation: Well done! The cork acts as a tight lid, making sure all the warm steam is forced to travel upward through the central tube and out the mouthpiece where the patient needs it.

question: When listening to music, what property of a sound wave tells you whether the note is high or low (pitch)?

options.A: Resonance
options.B: Frequency
options.C: Amplitude
options.D: Velocity

explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz and determines the pitch of a sound. Think of high-frequency sounds as high-pitched, like a baby crying, and low-frequency as deep, like a drum!

question: During which major conflicts did helicopters first become popular for rapid medical evacuation?

options.A: The American Civil War
options.B: World War I
options.C: The Korean and Vietnam Wars
options.D: World War II

explanation: Great job! Helicopters really changed wartime nursing during the Korean and Vietnam wars, helping nurses reach injured soldiers much closer to the front lines.

question: What is the trick to using a penlight sideways (tangential lighting) during a skin check?

options.A: To cast shadows that highlight the elevation or depression of a skin lesion
options.B: To sterilize the immediate area surrounding an open wound
options.C: To measure the exact surface area diameter of a chronic skin ulcer
options.D: To warm up cold skin before checking the patient's overall turgor

explanation: Shining the light from the side creates helpful shadows. This makes bumps, lumps, or dents much easier to spot!

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important for a maternal near-miss survivor?

options.A: It prevents her from developing high blood pressure in future years
options.B: Mental health counseling helps her uterus contract back to normal size
options.C: She is at high risk for post-traumatic stress disorder and depression
options.D: Psychological therapy is required to restore normal blood hemoglobin levels

explanation: Coming that close to death leaves deep emotional scars. Checking in on her mental well-being is just as important as checking her physical vitals!

question: A patient complains of chest pain and trouble swallowing because their food pipe is squeezing in an uncoordinated way. What is this called?

options.A: Oesophageal varices
options.B: Hiatus hernia
options.C: Oesophageal spasm
options.D: Mallory-Weiss tear

explanation: Correct! When the muscles of the oesophagus contract in a chaotic, painful squeeze rather than smooth waves, it's called an oesophageal spasm.

question: Why is working closely with local and religious leaders so vital for successful immunization drives?

options.A: Village leaders are trained to administer routine injections during staff shortages
options.B: Community members fund the importation of foreign vaccine supplies
options.C: Trusted local voices help address fears and clear up cultural misconceptions about vaccines
options.D: Local leaders inspect refrigerator temperatures every morning before clinic opens

explanation: People trust their community leaders. When elders and local leaders support immunization, families feel safe and eager to bring their children forward!

question: Where does the circulating nurse work during a surgical procedure?

options.A: Outside the sterile field, managing room coordination and documentation
options.B: Inside the sterile field, handling surgical instruments directly
options.C: In the hospital pharmacy preparing medications
options.D: In the recovery ward away from the surgical suite

explanation: Well done! The circulating nurse stays unscrubbed and moves around outside the sterile zone to coordinate and handle records.

question: Which type of shock is caused by a massive loss of blood or body fluids?

options.A: Obstructive shock
options.B: Neurogenic shock
options.C: Hypovolemic shock
options.D: Cardiogenic shock

explanation: Hypovolemic shock directly stems from a low volume of circulating blood or fluid inside the vascular system. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why might a surgeon choose external fixation over a standard internal plate for a severe open fracture?

options.A: It allows the patient to remove the metal pins at home every evening
options.B: It avoids placing metal hardware directly into a contaminated wound area
options.C: It completely eliminates any need for follow-up X-ray imaging
options.D: It guarantees that the bone will heal twice as fast as internal surgery

explanation: External frames hold bones securely from the outside, minimizing the risk of trapping bacteria and deep infection inside a dirty open wound. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h5)

question: What is the main job of the chairperson during a professional meeting?

options.A: Serving refreshments to all invited attendees
options.B: Guiding discussion and keeping the team on the agenda
options.C: Taking over patient care duties while staff are away
options.D: Writing down every single word spoken by participants

explanation: The chairperson leads the session, manages time, and ensures the group sticks to the planned topics.

question: Why should a nurse pay attention to family dynamics and community decision-makers?

options.A: So the nurse can bypass the patient entirely and speak only to community elders
options.B: To legally transfer medical decision-making rights away from the patient
options.C: To report family members who disagree with modern medical practices to the police
options.D: Because family heads or spouses often influence whether a patient seeks or continues treatment

explanation: Spot on! In many Nigerian communities, family and elders play a massive role in health choices, so winning their support helps the patient heal.

question: Which body area absorbs topical medications the fastest, often requiring a lower concentration?

options.A: The face and skin folds
options.B: The soles of the feet
options.C: The palms of the hands
options.D: The thick skin of the back

explanation: Thin skin areas absorb medications much quicker, increasing the risk of irritation if the drug is too strong. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h2)

question: How do bad roads and insecurity impact the work of voluntary health agencies?

options.A: They increase the number of qualified volunteer doctors
options.B: They stop community members from falling sick
options.C: They make it difficult to deliver medical supplies safely
options.D: They improve the distribution of government funds

explanation: You got it! Bad roads and security risks make traveling to remote areas a dangerous and stressful chore for healthcare teams.

question: Why is it important to talk about contraception early after birth, even before periods return?

options.A: Hormonal changes permanently stop ovulation for at least one year
options.B: Lactation guarantees complete protection against any future pregnancy
options.C: Menstruation always returns exactly six weeks after delivery
options.D: Fertility can return before the first postpartum menstrual period

explanation: Ovulation often happens before a mother sees her first period after birth. Knowing this helps us guide new mums safely!

question: Why should a nurse avoid performing blind finger sweeps when clearing an airway obstruction?

options.A: It causes severe bleeding inside the oral cavity
options.B: It can push the foreign object deeper into the airway
options.C: It breaks the patient's lower teeth and gums
options.D: It triggers an irreversible spasm of the vocal cords

explanation: Blind finger sweeps risk jamming a loose object further down the throat, making the blockage worse. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h7)

question: What is the best way to handle leftover cooked rice to keep bacteria from multiplying rapidly?

options.A: Add cold water and leave it sitting on the counter
options.B: Leave the pot covered tightly on the stove overnight
options.C: Refrigerate the leftover rice promptly in shallow containers
options.D: Store it warm in a sealed plastic bag in a dark cupboard

explanation: You got it! Cooling food quickly in shallow dishes gets it out of the danger zone where bacteria love to throw a party. Fantastic job today!

question: Why is giving people only cheap, starchy food not enough for long-term health?

options.A: It cannot be stored in community kitchens
options.B: It causes immediate starvation within a few hours
options.C: It is always more expensive than fresh vegetables
options.D: It does not prevent micronutrient deficiencies or hidden hunger

explanation: Well reasoned! While starch gives energy, true health needs a balance of vitamins, minerals, and proteins to keep deficiency diseases away.

question: What is the primary purpose of advance care planning?

options.A: To allow patients to state their medical wishes before they lose decision-making capacity
options.B: To reduce hospital liability in case of accidental patient falls
options.C: To guarantee that a patient receives aggressive life support under all circumstances
options.D: To transfer financial assets to family members before passing away

explanation: Advance care planning lets individuals guide their future healthcare treatment when they are no longer able to speak or make decisions for themselves. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h6)

question: Why is it important to ask about past surgical complications, such as a bad reaction to anesthesia?

options.A: To calculate the exact hospital bill in advance
options.B: To check if the patient has valid health insurance
options.C: To prevent similar dangerous reactions during future procedures
options.D: To determine what food the patient likes to eat

explanation: Knowing about previous adverse anesthesia reactions allows the surgical and anesthesia team to take safety precautions. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which kitchen tool is notorious for trapping wheat crumbs and causing cross-contamination?

options.A: Stainless steel pots used for boiling water
options.B: Toasters used for regular wheat bread
options.C: Ceramic dinner plates washed in hot water
options.D: Glass storage bowls with tight plastic lids

explanation: Toasters hold onto bread crumbs inside their heating coils, making them nearly impossible to clean completely for someone with celiac disease.

question: Which UN number is typically used for routine diagnostic specimens classified as Category B biological substances?
explanation: Think of UN 3373 as the standard code you see on diamond labels for everyday lab samples like blood tubes. Easy to remember once you spot it a few times!

question: Which signs and symptoms usually show up first when a person is coming down with Ebola?

options.A: Sudden fever, fatigue, and severe muscle aches
options.B: Profuse internal bleeding and skin bruising
options.C: Paralysis of the lower limbs and blindness
options.D: Productive cough and severe chest congestion

explanation: You nailed it! Early Ebola can easily feel like malaria or typhoid at first—sudden fever and body weakness are the major clues.

question: Why is community outreach by nurses and midwives so vital for family planning programs?

options.A: It helps engage local leaders and dismantle cultural stigma against modern methods.
options.B: It allows health workers to bypass government health policies entirely.
options.C: It ensures that nurses can collect financial levies from local households.
options.D: It replaces the need for clinical examinations inside health facilities.

explanation: Spot on! Going out into the community builds trust, involves local leaders, and helps clear up cultural or religious worries right at the grassroots level.

question: Why is creating a warm, non-judgmental environment so essential in family planning nursing?

options.A: It guarantees that no client will ever experience any side effects
options.B: It encourages clients to be honest and seek care without fear
options.C: It forces every community member to use the exact same method
options.D: It eliminates the need for any documentation in client files

explanation: When clients feel safe and unjudged, they tell the truth about their health and keep coming back for care. That is the heart of nursing!

question: How does a non-judgmental attitude from a nurse directly improve reproductive healthcare outcomes?

options.A: It allows the clinic to reduce its security staff budget
options.B: It guarantees that the client will never experience medical complications
options.C: It speeds up the discharge process for postpartum mothers
options.D: It encourages clients to share accurate history and seek help early

explanation: When clients feel accepted rather than judged, they are more honest about their symptoms and seek care before problems escalate. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h5)

question: A patient cannot shrug their right shoulder or turn their head properly. Which nerve might be damaged?

options.A: Accessory nerve
options.B: Abducens nerve
options.C: Oculomotor nerve
options.D: Trochlear nerve

explanation: That's correct! The accessory nerve (CN XI) powers the neck and shoulder muscles we use to turn our head and lift our shoulders.

question: When measuring how long an NG tube needs to be, what do the letters NEX stand for?

options.A: Neck to Esophagus to Xiphoid
options.B: Naris to Epiglottis to X-ray
options.C: Nose to Earlobe to Xiphoid process
options.D: Nose to Eye to X-ray

explanation: N-E-X stands for Nose to Earlobe to Xiphoid process. It's the classic bedside trick to estimate the exact length needed to reach the stomach.

question: Why are young women biologically more vulnerable to catching sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Faster overall blood circulation to the lower abdomen
options.B: Increased acidity of the normal vaginal flora
options.C: A higher resting body temperature in the pelvic region
options.D: The large area of mucous membrane in the reproductive tract

explanation: Think of the delicate lining inside the female reproductive tract—it has a large surface area that makes it easy for bacteria and viruses to settle in.

question: If a nurse is explaining a new handwashing study to a local community group, how should they share the message?

options.A: Present detailed statistical p-values and regression analyses
options.B: Provide dense theoretical frameworks for academic peer review
options.C: Use clear, jargon-free health education explaining personal wellbeing
options.D: Focus strictly on hospital budget allocations and administrative policy

explanation: Well done! Everyday patients and community members need simple, practical information without any heavy academic terms.

question: What sign tells you a patient is struggling and working extra hard to breathe?

options.A: Warm and dry skin on the forehead
options.B: Use of accessory neck and chest muscles
options.C: Symmetrical and slow chest wall rise
options.D: Quiet and relaxed abdominal movement

explanation: When breathing gets tough, the neck and shoulder muscles kick in to help pull air in. Watch those shoulders!

question: Why must everyone step back and not touch the patient while the AED is analyzing?

options.A: Movement can interfere with accurate rhythm analysis by the device
options.B: To prevent the rescuer from getting accidentally shocked
options.C: It gives the resuscitation team more physical room to work
options.D: Touching the patient increases the electrical output of the machine

explanation: Any motion or shaking can trick the smart computer inside the AED into misreading the heart rhythm. Staying clear keeps the reading accurate!

question: How does endocrine signaling mostly differ from the nervous system?

options.A: Endocrine organs use ducts to release chemicals.
options.B: Nervous responses use hormones instead of electricity.
options.C: Endocrine responses are slower and last longer.
options.D: Nervous signals target every cell in the body at once.

explanation: You got it! While nervous system signals flash by in a split second, endocrine signals travel through the blood and take their time to create lasting effects.

question: What is a major public health win when family planning services improve across Nigeria?

options.A: Reducing maternal and infant mortality rates
options.B: Guaranteed economic wealth for every household
options.C: Eliminating all infectious diseases in children
options.D: Removing the need for primary health care clinics

explanation: Proper birth spacing gives mothers and babies a fighting chance at better health, directly lowering maternal and infant deaths. Beautiful impact of nursing care!

question: Which part of a sterile syringe must a nurse avoid touching to maintain proper aseptic technique?

options.A: The inner barrel and the plunger shaft
options.B: The outer colored flange of the syringe
options.C: The paper packaging before it is opened
options.D: The outside plastic wall of the barrel

explanation: Touching parts of the syringe that will contact medication or enter the sterile pathway introduces germs directly into the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why does a cut or break in the skin raise a patient's risk of getting sick?

options.A: Harmful germs can slip straight into the body without any barrier.
options.B: Langerhans cells stop working during healing.
options.C: Skin oil production increases so much that it traps bacteria.
options.D: The skin stops sweating, causing internal organs to overheat.

explanation: Great job! A whole skin barrier blocks germs effortlessly; once that barrier breaks, microbes have an open doorway into deeper tissues. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why do babies born to teenage mothers face higher risks of developmental delays?

options.A: Complete absence of breast milk production in teenagers
options.B: Mandatory separation of mother and child at birth
options.C: A combination of physical prematurity and the mother's limited caregiving maturity
options.D: Automatic genetic mutations caused by young maternal age

explanation: You got it! Being born early plays a part, and young mothers may also need extra guidance on caring for a baby as they grow.

question: In a published research paper, where can you usually find recommendations for future studies?

options.A: In the author biography section
options.B: Among the financial sponsorship disclosures
options.C: At the end of the article
options.D: Inside the abstract summary

explanation: Researchers love to wrap up their papers by pointing out what still needs to be explored. Always check the conclusion section!

question: What is the best way to help prevent slips and falls in the bathroom?

options.A: Removing grab bars to increase arm movement
options.B: Applying heavy floor wax to make tiles shine
options.C: Placing non-slip mats on wet tub and shower surfaces
options.D: Turning off bathroom lights to reduce glare

explanation: Non-slip mats give great traction on slippery tiles when soap and water are around. It's a quick win for patient safety!

question: Why do people lose weight so fast in the first few days of a strict fad diet?

options.A: Instantaneous healing of the gastrointestinal lining
options.B: Permanent destruction of abnormal fat cells in the abdomen
options.C: Loss of body water and breakdown of stored muscle protein
options.D: Rapid increase in physical activity levels induced by supplements

explanation: That quick drop on the scale isn't fat—it's mostly water weight and muscle glycogen being used up. Good to know as a future nurse!

question: Why does the actual amount of oxygen (FiO2) a patient receives from a nasal cannula vary from person to person?

options.A: Different hospitals calibrate their wall oxygen outlets to different pressures
options.B: It depends on the patient's breathing rate and depth, which mixes room air with the oxygen
options.C: Patients absorb oxygen at different speeds through their skin
options.D: The plastic tubing stretches or shrinks based on the room temperature

explanation: Because a nasal cannula is an open system, patients breathe in regular room air right along with the oxygen. How fast or deep they breathe changes the exact mix!

question: What happens when the internal urethral sphincter relaxes during normal urination?

options.A: The kidneys immediately start producing a fresh batch of urine.
options.B: Semen is forced backward into the bladder instead of moving forward.
options.C: The pelvic floor muscles contract violently to push out the remaining waste.
options.D: Urine is allowed to flow out of the bladder into the upper urethra.

explanation: Spot on! Relaxing this internal muscle opens the bladder neck so urine can begin its journey down.

question: Why is it important to keep cardboard safety boxes away from damp floors?

options.A: Moisture helps safety boxes assemble themselves
options.B: Water makes the needles inside sharper and safer
options.C: Wet cardboard attracts helpful insects to the room
options.D: Dampness weakens the cardboard and causes dangerous leaks

explanation: That's right! Water ruins cardboard rigidity, which can lead to nasty punctures or fluid leaks from used sharps.

question: When smooth muscle is getting ready to contract, which protein does calcium bind to?

options.A: Calmodulin
options.B: Myosin light chain kinase
options.C: Tropomyosin
options.D: Troponin

explanation: Since smooth muscle doesn't use troponin like skeletal muscle does, it relies on a helpful protein called calmodulin to spot calcium and kick off the contraction.

question: Which specific antidote is given for a paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose?

options.A: Activated charcoal
options.B: Protamine sulfate
options.C: Naloxone hydrochloride
options.D: N-acetylcysteine

explanation: N-acetylcysteine (often called NAC) is the lifesaving go-to for paracetamol overdoses. It restores liver protectors (glutathione) just in time to save the liver cells.

question: Why is it a good idea to brainstorm several different options before making a final management decision?

options.A: It ensures that every staff member gets promoted
options.B: It prevents settling prematurely on a poor solution
options.C: It makes the decision-making process instantaneous
options.D: It eliminates the need to evaluate costs

explanation: Looking at multiple alternatives stops you from jumping blindly at the very first idea that pops into your head.

question: Why did the Alma-Ata Declaration emphasize intersectoral collaboration for health?

options.A: Because doctors need help from corporate business owners to run pharmacies
options.B: Because factors like housing, education, and agriculture directly influence community health
options.C: Because hospital administrators wanted to share their paperwork with local schools
options.D: Because nurses must learn how to farm to provide proper nutrition advice

explanation: Health is shaped by social and environmental factors outside the clinic, requiring teamwork across different societal sectors. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the key feature of appropriate technology in primary health care?

options.A: It relies entirely on uninterrupted electrical power grids
options.B: It requires a university degree to operate safely
options.C: It must be imported directly from advanced industrial nations
options.D: It is affordable, culturally acceptable, and easy to maintain locally

explanation: Appropriate technology must fit the local context, meaning it is affordable, sustainable, and accepted by the community. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h6)

question: What crucial instruction should a nurse give a patient taking prescribed corticosteroid therapy?

options.A: Stop the medication immediately if you start to feel better
options.B: Never stop taking the medication suddenly without medical guidance
options.C: Increase your daily salt intake to balance the steroid effects
options.D: Take the pills on an empty stomach right before bedtime

explanation: Abruptly stopping steroids can trigger a dangerous adrenal crisis because the body stops producing its own natural stress hormones during treatment. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to teamwork across sectors in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive funding and immediate budget releases for all health programs
options.B: Sectoral sidelining and agencies operating in isolation
options.C: Bureaucratic red tape between different government tiers
options.D: Frequent changes in local political leadership

explanation: You got it! Chronic underfunding and delayed budgets are huge hurdles—we definitely don't have the problem of 'too much money'!

question: How is cholera primarily passed to humans?

options.A: Through direct skin-to-skin contact
options.B: Through contaminated water and food
options.C: By inhaling airborne respiratory droplets
options.D: Via the bite of infected mosquitoes

explanation: Swallowing water or food polluted with tiny traces of waste is how the bacteria enters our digestive system. Good hygiene stops it!

question: Which professional is best suited to help community nurses promote backyard farming?

options.A: Hospital biomedical engineer
options.B: Surgical theater technician
options.C: Emergency room pharmacist
options.D: Agricultural extension worker

explanation: Agricultural workers have the expertise in crop growing and farming techniques needed to support backyard gardens. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h7)

question: What is the main job of Ethambutol when given with other TB medications?

options.A: Destroying the liver enzymes that break down other drugs
options.B: Killing all dormant bacteria within the first week
options.C: Preventing the emergence of bacterial resistance
options.D: Relieving joint pains caused by pyrazinamide

explanation: Ethambutol acts as a solid backup team member, stopping the bacteria from building resistance while the other drugs do the heavy lifting.

question: Why is it helpful to have colleagues review your research report before submitting it?

options.A: Colleagues can catch errors and blind spots that the author missed
options.B: It guarantees that the research paper will win academic awards
options.C: It allows someone else to take full credit for the study
options.D: It eliminates the need for any references or citations

explanation: When you stare at your own writing for hours, you miss tiny mistakes. Fresh eyes help spot typos and confusing parts!

question: What common problem can happen if a patient wears a poorly fitted prosthetic limb?

options.A: Skin breakdown and pressure ulcers
options.B: Complete recovery of muscle strength
options.C: Rapid elevation of blood pressure
options.D: Sudden permanent loss of vision

explanation: Friction from ill-fitting gear is tough on fragile skin and can quickly lead to painful sores. Good nursing assessment catches this early!

question: What is a key responsibility for a nurse right after a screening test is completed?

options.A: Explaining how and when the client will get their results
options.B: Telling the client to stop seeing all other doctors
options.C: Destroying all records of the patient visit immediately
options.D: Prescribing strong medications before results come out

explanation: Spot on! Patients always need to know when and how to expect their findings so they can follow up properly.

question: What makes chlorhexidine gluconate a popular antiseptic choice in the theatre?

options.A: It works instantly with zero contact time
options.B: It kills viruses faster than any other chemical
options.C: It is easily washed away by hard water
options.D: It keeps fighting bacteria and prevents growth for hours

explanation: Chlorhexidine is great because it binds to your skin and keeps working long after you've finished scrubbing!

question: A nurse compares the number of malaria cases between two villages with different population sizes. Why is calculating a rate better than just looking at raw counts?

options.A: Rates eliminate the need for laboratory confirmations
options.B: Raw counts are always illegal to use in public health
options.C: Rates account for differences in total population size
options.D: Raw counts are harder to write down on paper forms

explanation: Comparing raw counts alone can be misleading if one village is much larger than the other; rates provide a fair comparison. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h5)

question: What major reproductive problem is linked to fallopian tube scarring from untreated pelvic infections?

options.A: Premature menopause
options.B: Hypertrophic cervical polyps
options.C: Endometrial hyperplasia
options.D: Ectopic pregnancy and infertility

explanation: Scars in the fallopian tubes can block eggs from traveling normally, leading either to trouble getting pregnant or dangerous ectopic pregnancies.

question: Which chemical messenger (neurotransmitter) is released by almost all autonomic preganglionic nerve fibers?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Acetylcholine
options.C: Dopamine
options.D: Norepinephrine

explanation: Acetylcholine is the go-to chemical messenger used at the first synapse (ganglion) for both the sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions. Great job!

question: What is a major focus of donor-supported family planning programs in primary health clinics?

options.A: Mandating contraceptive use for all married couples
options.B: Building private hospitals in every rural community
options.C: Replacing all local doctors with foreign medical experts
options.D: Preventing commodity stock-outs and training health staff

explanation: These programs focus heavily on making sure clinics never run out of supplies and helping local healthcare workers build their clinical skills.

question: Which of these tasks is NOT part of a nurse's daily responsibilities when dealing with LFTs?

options.A: Monitoring the blood draw site for bleeding afterward
options.B: Diagnosing the specific stage of cirrhosis from the lab slip
options.C: Ensuring proper patient preparation and fasting if required
options.D: Checking patient medication history for drugs that stress the liver

explanation: That's right! We prep the patient, check medications, and keep them safe, but making the final disease diagnosis is the doctor's job.

question: Which of these is NOT a good reason to avoid using leftover antibiotics for a new cold?

options.A: Colds are usually caused by viruses, which antibiotics cannot kill
options.B: Using leftover drugs can lead to incorrect dosing and drug resistance
options.C: Leftover antibiotics are guaranteed to work faster than fresh prescriptions
options.D: Sharing drugs promotes dangerous resistance patterns in the community

explanation: That's right! Leftover drugs are never a magic shortcut; using them wrongly for viral colds is useless and dangerous.

question: A nurse notices a sudden rise in wound infections on the surgical ward. What makes surveillance data valuable here?

options.A: It proves that surgery should be temporarily stopped
options.B: It helps identify a pattern to stop further infections
options.C: It allows the nurse to blame the cleaning staff
options.D: It ensures the patients get discharged faster

explanation: Tracking infection patterns gives clues about the source so corrective action can happen fast. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h2)

question: Which of these is a very common physical hazard you might find in a patient's home?

options.A: Standardized hospital call bells in every room
options.B: Sterile, bolted-down medical furniture
options.C: Continuous negative pressure isolation airflow
options.D: Frayed electrical cords and loose throw rugs

explanation: Everyday household items like loose rugs and damaged cords are top culprits for trips and falls in residential settings. Always watch out for them!

question: What simple administrative step helps stop children from disappearing into trafficking rings?

options.A: Banning travel between states
options.B: Mandatory military service
options.C: Closing local primary schools
options.D: Universal birth registration

explanation: Official birth records give a child a legal identity, making it much harder for traffickers to move them around unnoticed.

question: What is the number one symptom patients with vulval inflammation usually report?

options.A: Intense itching
options.B: Excessive hair growth
options.C: Severe bone pain
options.D: Complete numbness

explanation: Pruritus, which is just the medical word for itching, is almost always the main complaint when a patient has vulvitis. You're building solid clinical instincts!

question: What is a key policy step needed to improve medication dispensing systems nationally?

options.A: Making all prescription drugs completely free for every citizen
options.B: Transferring all nursing duties to the central pharmacy department
options.C: Banning the use of mobile carts in all public healthcare facilities
options.D: Including unit dose standards in hospital accreditation requirements

explanation: Enforcing standards through official accreditation ensures hospitals allocate necessary resources to maintain safe dispensing practices. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h8)

question: A patient keeps having seizures even after trying three different anti-seizure medications at maximum doses. What is the best next step to explore?

options.A: Discharging the patient to outpatient psychiatric care
options.B: Immediate cessation of all pharmacological treatment
options.C: Evaluation for possible resective epilepsy surgery
options.D: Switching to a fourth standard anti-seizure drug

explanation: When medications don't control the seizures, referring the patient to an epilepsy specialist center for surgical evaluation is a great next step.

question: What does the term 'food security' refer to in nutritional nursing assessments?

options.A: Having reliable access to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food
options.B: Eating only foods that have been certified organic by government agencies
options.C: Keeping hospital kitchen supplies locked away from pests
options.D: Storing perishable groceries at the correct refrigerator temperature

explanation: Food security means an individual has physical and economic access to the food they need for an active, healthy life. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h5)

question: Why does dangerously high pressure inside the skull cause changes in how a patient's pupils react?

options.A: It destroys the retina directly inside the eyeball
options.B: It compresses cranial nerve III against surrounding structures
options.C: It blocks light from entering the cornea
options.D: It stops blood flow to the tear ducts

explanation: When pressure builds up in the head, it pushes brain tissue down and squeezes Cranial Nerve III (the oculomotor nerve), which normally controls pupil size.

question: In financial management, what is a "variance"?

options.A: The variation in patient recovery times across different wards
options.B: The difference between budgeted amounts and actual financial outcomes
options.C: The total amount of profit made from pharmacy sales alone
options.D: The legal penalty given to hospitals for missing safety records

explanation: A variance is simply the gap between what you planned to spend in your budget and what you actually spent in reality.

question: A patient is recovering from a stroke and needs help with walking and swallowing. Who should be on this care team?

options.A: The pharmacist and the hospital security personnel only
options.B: Only the patient's family members making independent choices
options.C: The nurse, physiotherapist, speech therapist, and the patient
options.D: Only the attending physician and the hospital accountant

explanation: Exactly! Recovery takes a village—different specialists are needed to tackle different physical challenges alongside the patient.

question: Which pancreatic hormone is primarily responsible for lowering blood glucose levels?

options.A: Cortisol
options.B: Thyroxine
options.C: Glucagon
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Insulin facilitates the movement of glucose out of the bloodstream and into body cells, effectively lowering circulating blood sugar levels. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T5#GNS211_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the main idea behind 'standard precautions' in patient care?

options.A: Using protective gowns only during major surgical operations
options.B: Washing hands strictly after finishing a 12-hour hospital shift
options.C: Only wearing gloves when caring for patients with a diagnosed fever
options.D: Treating all body fluids from any patient as potentially infectious

explanation: Spot on! Standard precautions mean we treat everyone's body fluids as if they could carry an infection, keeping us safe every time.

question: Which nursing action is essential after chest surgery to prevent lung complications like pneumonia?

options.A: Keeping the patient completely immobile in bed for two weeks
options.B: Administering strong sleeping pills to eliminate night coughing
options.C: Restricting all oral fluid intake to keep the lungs completely dry
options.D: Encouraging deep breathing and the use of an incentive spirometer

explanation: Getting patients to take deep breaths and use an incentive spirometer expands their tiny air sacs (alveoli), keeping pneumonia and lung collapse away!

question: Why do nurses prefer IV medications over oral tablets during severe emergencies?

options.A: It is completely painless for the patient
options.B: It delivers medication directly into the bloodstream for fast action
options.C: Oral medications are illegal in hospital emergency units
options.D: It eliminates the need for any dosage calculations

explanation: IV meds skip the digestive system completely, hitting the bloodstream instantly when every single second counts.

question: Why do modern nurses prefer keeping a wound environment moist?

options.A: It leaves the wound completely open to fresh air safely.
options.B: It keeps the body from producing any fluid at all.
options.C: It stops all bacterial growth on the skin completely.
options.D: It lets skin cells repair faster and helps prevent harsh scarring.

explanation: Skin cells love moisture! They glide across a moist wound bed way faster than trying to crawl across a dry, crusty scab. Great nursing knowledge to keep in your pocket.

question: Why does a peri-operative nurse need both strong clinical skills and great communication?

options.A: Operating rooms prohibit verbal communication during procedures.
options.B: The nursing council mandates dual certification for all surgical staff.
options.C: Patients face high physical risks and emotional stress during surgery.
options.D: Surgeons require nurses to manage hospital administrative duties.

explanation: Surgery is a big deal! Patients and their families go through a lot of physical and emotional stress, so nurses need to be skilled and comforting.

question: A patient using axillary crutches complains of numbness and tingling in their fingers. What instruction should the nurse provide?

options.A: Switch immediately to using a standard four-wheeled walker
options.B: Adjust the crutches so they fit higher up in the armpit
options.C: Lean your upper body forward to relieve hand pressure
options.D: Support your body weight on your hands, not your armpits

explanation: Resting body weight on the armpits compresses nerves and blood vessels, leading to nerve damage and tingling; weight must go through the hand grips. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h4)

question: Why do frontline nurses sometimes resist monitoring and quality controls from their managers?

options.A: They prefer spending their entire shift filling out paper incident logs
options.B: They believe hospital administrators want patient care standards to be low
options.C: They may view the controls as micromanagement and a sign of mistrust
options.D: They are legally forbidden from participating in quality improvement

explanation: If monitoring isn't explained well, staff can feel spied on rather than supported, leading to pushback against helpful safety checks.

question: How does the body's immune system play a role in letting endometriosis develop?

options.A: It causes an overproduction of red blood cells during menses
options.B: It produces antibodies that destroy normal uterine muscle tissue
options.C: It fails to clear misplaced endometrial cells from the pelvic cavity
options.D: It permanently blocks the normal release of estrogen and progesterone

explanation: Normally, our immune system cleans up stray cells. In endometriosis, the local immune defense drops the ball, allowing those stray cells to stick around and grow.

question: A nurse notices a husband is dominating the conversation and suspects his wife is hiding health issues. What is the best first step?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately and document that care was refused
options.B: Scold the husband in front of the patient for interrupting the health history
options.C: Refuse to let the husband enter the clinic room during future appointments
options.D: Create a moment to speak with the patient privately without the husband present

explanation: Always find a safe moment—like stepping out for a lab test or a quick bathroom break—to talk with the patient alone so she feels safe to share what's really going on.

question: Why is frequent mouth care essential for a patient with a nasogastric tube?

options.A: Saliva production increases to dangerous levels with a tube
options.B: Toothpaste helps dissolve the adhesive tape on the nose
options.C: Oral hygiene prevents the tube from clogging with food
options.D: Mouth breathing dries out oral mucous membranes quickly

explanation: Having a tube in the nose forces the patient to breathe through the mouth, causing dryness, pain, and cracking. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h7)

question: Based on how much the body needs them, what are the two main groups of nutrients?

options.A: Macronutrients and micronutrients
options.B: Proteins and carbohydrates
options.C: Organic and inorganic nutrients
options.D: Vitamins and minerals

explanation: You got this! We split nutrients into macronutrients (needed in large amounts like carbs and proteins) and micronutrients (needed in small amounts like vitamins).

question: Which factor is a common logistical barrier to emergency referrals in rural communities?

options.A: An excessive surplus of functional ambulances
options.B: Poor road networks and lack of reliable transport
options.C: Too many specialists working in primary health posts
options.D: Free fuel supplies provided by local youth groups

explanation: Bad roads and lack of vehicles often delay the physical transfer of emergency patients to higher facilities. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h7)

question: What do the letters in the CAGE questionnaire stand for?

options.A: Control, Addicted, Grief, Escape
options.B: Crave, Anxiety, Guilt, Energy loss
options.C: Count, Assess, Guide, Evaluate
options.D: Cut down, Annoyed, Guilty, Eye-opener

explanation: The CAGE acronym helps clinicians remember four quick screening questions about cutting down, annoyance, guilt, and morning drinking. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h5)

question: During which stages of pregnancy do women usually need an extra 340 to 450 calories every day?

options.A: The first two weeks after conception
options.B: First trimester only
options.C: During labor and delivery
options.D: Second and third trimesters

explanation: As that little baby starts growing super fast in the later months, the mother needs a small energy boost of extra daily calories!

question: How do you correctly straighten an adult's ear canal before flushing it?

options.A: Push the tragus inward over the opening
options.B: Tilt the head sharply toward the chest
options.C: Pull the earlobe straight downward
options.D: Pull the outer ear (pinna) upward and backward

explanation: For adults, pulling the pinna up and back straightens out the curvy ear canal so your water stream can reach the blockage easily.

question: Which class of blood pressure medication works primarily by helping the kidneys remove excess water and sodium from the body?

options.A: Diuretics
options.B: Statins
options.C: Antibiotics
options.D: Beta-blockers

explanation: Diuretics, or water pills, prompt the kidneys to excrete sodium and water, reducing overall blood volume and pressure. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of injection safety in clinical practice?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing disposable syringes
options.B: To speed up medication administration during busy ward shifts
options.C: To ensure patients experience zero pain during every procedure
options.D: To prevent harm to patients, healthcare workers, and the community

explanation: Injection safety encompasses protective measures for everyone involved in or affected by the injection process, preventing infections and injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT part of a standard school health program?

options.A: Health instruction and education
options.B: School health services
options.C: Advanced neurosurgical training
options.D: Healthy school environment

explanation: Correct! Brain surgery is specialized hospital care, way beyond what a primary school health program needs or does.

question: Why do healthcare workers perform an Allen test before drawing an arterial blood gas (ABG) sample?

options.A: To verify adequate collateral circulation to the hand
options.B: To numb the puncture site before inserting the needle
options.C: To measure the exact blood pressure in the radial artery
options.D: To check if the patient has a bleeding disorder

explanation: The Allen test makes sure the hand has a backup blood supply (from the ulnar artery) just in case the radial artery gets blocked during the needle puncture.

question: What is the primary cause of hereditary conditions?

options.A: Exposure to common bacterial infections
options.B: Changes in the DNA sequence
options.C: Inadequate nutrition during pregnancy
options.D: Poor personal hygiene during childhood

explanation: Hereditary conditions stem directly from genetic mutations or alterations passed down from parents to their offspring. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h1)

question: Why is finding out if a mother is Rhesus-negative during her first visit so crucial?

options.A: It proves the mother has adequate iron levels in her blood
options.B: It guarantees the baby will never develop newborn jaundice
options.C: It allows the nurse to schedule the exact day of delivery
options.D: It helps prevent potential blood incompatibility and isoimmunization

explanation: Catching a Rhesus-negative blood type early lets you plan ahead for special care (like anti-D injections) to keep both current and future babies safe!

question: What is the typical length of a normal menstrual cycle for an adult woman?

options.A: 40 to 50 days
options.B: 60 to 75 days
options.C: 21 to 35 days
options.D: 10 to 14 days

explanation: While textbooks love talking about a 28-day cycle, any cycle that consistently falls between 21 and 35 days is completely normal and healthy!

question: How are Dietary Reference Intakes (DRIs) usually used in everyday practice?

options.A: To treat acute vitamin toxicity in emergency rooms
options.B: To plan and evaluate nutrient intakes for healthy populations
options.C: To calculate exact medication dosages for surgical patients
options.D: To diagnose rare metabolic genetic diseases

explanation: DRIs give nurses and dietitians a helpful baseline to check if healthy groups are getting the right amount of nutrients.

question: Why is proper nursing documentation so legally critical for patient care?

options.A: It allows patients to diagnose their own illnesses at home
options.B: It serves as a legal record proving what care was delivered to the patient
options.C: It replaces the need for nurses to talk to doctors in person
options.D: It guarantees that the hospital will receive extra government funding

explanation: Remember the golden rule in nursing: if you didn't chart it, you didn't do it! Your notes are legal proof of the safe care you provided.

question: Why must a patient take off their daily nitroglycerin skin patch for a few hours every day?

options.A: To prevent the patch from falling off in the shower
options.B: To stop severe skin irritation from the adhesive
options.C: To prevent the body from developing drug tolerance
options.D: To allow the blood pressure to rise back to normal

explanation: Giving the body a daily break from nitrates (a nitrate-free interval) keeps the medication working effectively so the body doesn't just get used to it and ignore it.

question: A pregnant woman experiences chronic malnutrition late in pregnancy. Which nutrient transfer process is most likely to be affected first regarding fetal bone development?

options.A: Pinocytosis of maternal immunoglobulins
options.B: Active transport of minerals like calcium
options.C: Simple diffusion of respiratory oxygen
options.D: Facilitated diffusion of free water

explanation: Minerals like calcium require active transport mechanisms powered by energy to build up in the fetal skeleton, which can be strained under severe maternal nutritional deficits. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h5)

question: When is radiation therapy usually added to a patient's treatment plan for vulval tumours?

options.A: Only to prevent normal hair from growing back on the labia
options.B: As the absolute first choice for tiny benign cysts
options.C: To replace the need for any diagnostic skin biopsies
options.D: For advanced cases or when surgery is not a safe option

explanation: Correct! Radiation is typically used when the cancer has spread too far for simple surgery, or if the patient's health makes surgery too risky.

question: Which of these is NOT a requirement for the Lactational Amenorrhea Method (LAM) to work safely?

options.A: The baby must be exclusively breastfed
options.B: The infant must be older than one year
options.C: The infant must be under six months of age
options.D: The mother must not have resumed menstruation

explanation: LAM is a temporary method that only works for the first six months after birth, as long as breastfeeding is exclusive and periods haven't returned.

question: What is the most common cause of anaemia in pregnant women everywhere?

options.A: Vitamin B12 deficiency
options.B: Autoimmune destruction
options.C: Acute blood loss
options.D: Iron deficiency

explanation: You nailed it. Because the growing baby and placenta need a lot of iron, mothers can easily run low if their diet or supplements don't keep up.

question: Where do most of our cranial nerves take their origin?

options.A: The brainstem
options.B: The cerebral cortex
options.C: The cerebellum
options.D: The spinal cord

explanation: Great job! While spinal nerves come from the spinal cord, most cranial nerves sprout right from the brainstem.

question: When you gently feel (palpate) a mother's tummy to check her uterus after birth, what is your main goal?

options.A: To confirm that the uterus is firm and contracting
options.B: To check if the bladder is completely empty
options.C: To stimulate milk production in the breasts
options.D: To measure the exact weight of the mother

explanation: A nice, hard, contracted uterus (like a firm mango!) stops bleeding. If it feels soft or boggy, that's a red flag for postpartum hemorrhage.

question: Why are home modifications like building ramps and widening doors often a major financial challenge?

options.A: Assistive devices mean you never need home alterations
options.B: Building codes make structural changes illegal
options.C: They require specialized labor and materials that insurance rarely covers
options.D: Modified homes cause higher utility bills

explanation: Renovating a house to make it wheelchair-accessible takes cash upfront. Because health insurance in our setting rarely covers home repairs, families carry the burden alone.

question: Why should you advise a client NOT to massage her arm or buttock after a DMPA injection?

options.A: It pushes the liquid medicine directly into a blood vessel
options.B: It speeds up drug absorption and shortens protection
options.C: It stops the needle puncture wound from closing properly
options.D: It causes severe bruising on the skin surface

explanation: Massaging increases blood flow, making the body absorb the hormone too fast. That means it might wear off sooner than expected!

question: What is the term for a patient's right to make independent decisions about their own medical treatment?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Negligence
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Malpractice

explanation: Correct! Autonomy simply means self-rule—giving every competent patient the full right to make their own healthcare choices.

question: How can pregnant women hold onto extra water and sodium without their blood pressure shooting up?

options.A: Renal tubules stop working completely in the second trimester.
options.B: The heart pumps with a much weaker force.
options.C: Excess fluid is immediately stored in the amniotic sac.
options.D: Systemic vascular resistance decreases at the same time.

explanation: Blood vessels relax and widen during pregnancy, giving the extra fluid plenty of room so blood pressure stays nice and stable.

question: Which organ is most commonly hurt by severe idiosyncratic drug reactions?

options.A: The heart
options.B: The liver
options.C: The lungs
options.D: The brain

explanation: Since almost every drug we swallow passes through the liver for processing, the liver is sadly the most frequent target for serious idiosyncratic reactions.

question: Why is a renal ultrasound often ordered when evaluating a patient with sudden kidney failure?

options.A: To test how well the liver is metabolizing circulating medications
options.B: To measure the exact amount of protein lost in a 24-hour period
options.C: To check for physical blockages or structural causes of urine backup
options.D: To determine the precise percentage of red blood cells in circulation

explanation: An ultrasound provides a clear image of the kidneys and urinary tract, helping doctors quickly identify postrenal obstructions like stones or an enlarged prostate. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h4)

question: What does the practice of evidence-based nursing combine?

options.A: Traditional beliefs, trial and error, and personal opinions
options.B: Hospital policies, doctor preferences, and budget limits
options.C: Quick solutions, strict punishments, and administrative orders
options.D: Research evidence, clinical expertise, and patient values

explanation: Evidence-based practice merges scientific research, the nurse's professional judgment, and what matters most to the individual patient. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h4)

question: What are the main signs that a family caregiver is suffering from severe burnout?

options.A: A sudden desire to pursue advanced nursing degrees
options.B: Exhaustion, resentment, and emotional exhaustion
options.C: Improved physical strength and restful sleep patterns
options.D: Increased energy and excitement for daily tasks

explanation: Caring for others 24/7 is draining. When a caregiver is completely burnt out, they feel emotionally fried, bone-tired, and sometimes overwhelmed with resentment.

question: How do subjective and objective data team up during patient assessment?

options.A: Subjective data replaces the physical exam entirely
options.B: Objective data is gathered only by asking the patient what they feel
options.C: Subjective data provides history while objective data provides measurable findings
options.D: Subjective and objective data are completely unrelated processes

explanation: Think of it this way: subjective data is what the patient tells you (like 'my head hurts'), while objective data is what you measure or see yourself (like a high temperature). Together, they give the full picture!

question: Why should you use a clean spatula or tongue depressor when taking cream from a shared jar?

options.A: To spread the cream faster across the patient's skin
options.B: To measure the exact milligram dose required
options.C: To warm the cream up before touching the patient
options.D: To prevent introducing bacteria and contaminating the jar

explanation: Using a tool instead of your bare fingers stops germs from getting into the shared jar and causing future infections.

question: During an open irrigation, what must you do immediately after disconnecting the catheter and tubing?

options.A: Flush the drainage bag with hot tap water
options.B: Ask the patient to stand up and walk around
options.C: Clean the floor around the bed with bleach
options.D: Protect both exposed ends with sterile caps

explanation: Always keep it sterile! Covering those open tips stops stray germs from jumping onto the connectors and into your patient.

question: A patient with painful second-degree burns on both feet is admitted to your ward. Which bed accessory is a must-have for their comfort?

options.A: An air ring
options.B: A bed cradle
options.C: A bed block
options.D: A footboard

explanation: You got it! Burned skin cannot handle the heavy weight and friction of standard bedsheets, so a bed cradle is a lifesaver for pain relief and healing.

question: An older patient complains that food tastes bland. Which age-related change causes this?

options.A: Hyper-sensitivity of the tongue nerves
options.B: Rapid enlargement of the salivary glands
options.C: Increased production of stomach acid
options.D: Decline in taste buds and olfactory nerve function

explanation: Spot on! Losing taste buds and having a weaker sense of smell dulls the flavor of food, which is why older adults often lose their appetite.

question: Which agency sets and enforces the main federal regulations for skilled nursing facilities?

options.A: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA)
options.B: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
options.C: World Health Organization (WHO)
options.D: National Institutes of Health (NIH)

explanation: CMS oversees the federal rules and quality standards that certified skilled nursing facilities must follow. You're building a strong regulatory foundation!

question: Why is regular antenatal care attendance so important for catching problems like antepartum haemorrhage early?

options.A: It builds up thick blood volume reserves to prevent all shock
options.B: It completely stops the uterus from contracting before term
options.C: It allows early ultrasound identification of abnormal placental placement
options.D: It guarantees that the mother will never experience any spotting

explanation: Routine antenatal check-ups and scans help healthcare providers spot conditions like placenta praevia early so precautions can be set up before any bleeding starts. Awesome job completing this session!

question: A nurse smoothly moves from managing an IV drip in the ER to dressing a wound in the surgical ward. What is this nurse showing?

options.A: Avoidance of heavy patient workloads
options.B: Strict adherence to departmental silos
